classification.difficultyReason: Several linked decisions using the demonstrated definitions or procedures. Pages 42–43 establish subsets and equality irrespective of order; apply these to three elements.

content.prompt:
Given a set $X$, its $\mathit{power\ set}$, $\mathcal P(X)$, is the set containing all subsets of $X$. Write down $\mathcal P(X)$ for
$$X=\{x,y,z\}.$$

answer.worked:
List subsets with zero, one, two and three elements. Order within a subset does not matter.
$$\mathcal P(X)=\bigl\{\varnothing,\{x\},\{y\},\{z\},\{x,y\},\{x,z\},\{y,z\},\{x,y,z\}\bigr\}.$$
There are $1+3+3+1=8$ subsets.
